# glyf

> Open Source Visualization build tool to data pipeline.

glyf helps analytics engineers generate static dashboards from analytical projects.
It uses .ggsql chart files, dashboard YAML, analytical artifacts, DuckDB execution, and static HTML export. Its first integration reads dbt artifacts.

Install (PyPI package glyf-core, command glyf):

```bash
uv tool install glyf-core
glyf --version
```

Or, on macOS and Linux:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glyf-data/glyf/main/install.sh | sh
```

Key project files:

- dbt_project.yml: dbt project definition.
- glyf.yml: glyf paths and dashboard config.
- models/: dbt SQL models.
- target/manifest.json: dbt artifact used to resolve ref() and source().
- visualisations/*.ggsql: chart SQL plus visualisation directives.
- dashboards/*.yml: dashboard definitions and chart ordering.
- target/glyf/: generated compiled SQL, chart artifacts, dashboards, and exported site.

Scaffold workflow:

```bash
glyf init
glyf init --clean
```

Use init from a dbt project root. It creates glyf.yml when missing, creates visualisations/ and dashboards/, writes a starter .ggsql file, and writes a starter dashboard YAML file. Use --clean only when replacing the starter chart/dashboard files selected by the prompts.

Core workflow:

```bash
dbt build
glyf doctor
glyf validate
glyf render
glyf dashboard
glyf export
```

When running from outside the dbt project, pass:

```bash
glyf validate --project-dir path/to/dbt_project
```

Assistant workflow:

1. If visualisations/ or dashboards/ are missing, suggest glyf init or run it when the user asks for scaffolding.
2. Read dbt_project.yml, glyf.yml, models/, target/manifest.json, visualisations/, and dashboards/.
3. Create or update a .ggsql file under visualisations/.
4. Add the chart name to the relevant dashboard YAML under dashboards/.
5. Run glyf doctor, validate, render, and dashboard.
6. Report changed files, validation results, generated artifacts, and anything requiring human review.

Guardrails for agents:

- Do not edit dbt models unless the user asks for model changes.
- Use only supported glyf .ggsql directives and chart types.
- Keep chart SQL close to dbt model names and existing project conventions.
- Preserve dashboard YAML unless the requested change requires an update.
- Explain unresolved refs, missing target/manifest.json, missing chart files, and DuckDB execution errors directly.
